quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: No r sound in RP. Hold a steady central vowel with neutral lips; the tongue doesn't move.
quests.explanation: Long, central and steady. The short lower vowel would give 'bud'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is long, tense and central with neutral lips; /ʌ/ is short, lower and more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ea here is no trap: it spells a held, spread-lip vowel.
quests.explanation: Ea signals this vowel in 'dream' and 'team', though 'bread' shows it is no guarantee.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Weak -ing, -ish and -ic endings carry /ɪ/ and are never lengthened. Save the long, tense vowel for stressed syllables.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The set is named after this word: jaw wide, tongue forward.
quests.explanation: It is the keyword of its set. A half-open jaw would blur it with the neighbouring vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A self-check: rest a hand under your chin. The jaw should drop noticeably further for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Stressed first syllable. The u here is the common 'cut' type, not the rare 'put' type.
quests.explanation: Unrounded and central. The rounded short vowel belongs to a closed list that includes 'put' and 'full'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is back-ish and rounded, lips gently pursed; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded, with the jaw more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent r. The jaw stays wide and the lips neutral for as long as you hold the vowel.
quests.explanation: Long and open. The short rounded vowel would give 'cot'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is long, open and unrounded; /ɒ/ is short, open and lightly rounded.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Keep the jaw half open after the /pr/ cluster.
quests.explanation: Mid-front tongue and a modest jaw drop. A wider mouth would be the other vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so the only question is how high the front of the tongue rises.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ur spelling gives a long central vowel in RP. Hold it steady.
quests.explanation: Ur, ir and er all spell this vowel, so spelling is a better guide here than usual.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Hold /ɜː/ steadily with the tongue mid-central. /ʌ/ is lower and clipped.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The au spelling is consistent. Make an oval with the lips.
quests.explanation: Long and rounded. The short vowel belongs in 'toss'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If your /ɒ/ comes out too long, shorten it and open the jaw rather than rounding tighter.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The oo before th is long here. Push the lips forward and hold.
quests.explanation: Long and rounded. The th ending does not change the vowel, and a short loose vowel would sound wrong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Quick, open, lips a bit rounded: nothing long about it.
quests.explanation: Short and rounded. The long open vowel would be wrong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are open and back, so the lips are the main difference: neutral for /ɑː/, slightly rounded for /ɒ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Jaw nearly closed. 'Pin' needs a smaller mouth gap than 'pen'.
quests.explanation: A wider jaw would turn it into 'pen', so keep the gap small.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue height is the cue: /ɪ/ sits close to high front, /e/ is mid-front with the jaw about half open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and lazy, it doesn't hold. 'Bun' is not 'burn'.
quests.explanation: Short and open. The long tense vowel belongs in 'burn'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling will not decide: ir, er, ur, ear and wor- give /ɜː/, while u, o and ou usually give /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The oo before k often gives a short rounded vowel, as in 'book' and 'look'. Round slightly.
quests.explanation: Rounded lips and a short vowel. Remove the rounding and you lose it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Lip rounding separates them: rounded for /ʊ/, flat for /ʌ/. The jaw drops further for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: In RP, a before th is long and open, like in 'path'.
quests.explanation: A BATH word with the long vowel. Northern English accents use the short one, but this course follows RP.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is pushed forward for /æ/ and pulled back and down for /ɑː/. Feel the tongue root move.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open jaw with rounded lips. After /fr/ the vowel is short.
quests.explanation: Without lip rounding it would drift towards the central vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is back and open with slightly rounded lips; /ʌ/ is central and unrounded with neutral lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The wor- spelling is a trap: don't round the lips as you would for 'fork'.
quests.explanation: No lip rounding here. Round the lips and you get the vowel of 'fork'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is central with neutral or slightly spread lips; /ɔː/ is back with clearly rounded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open wide, tongue forward. It isn't 'sund'.
quests.explanation: A central vowel would make the mouth too small.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is front and low with a wide mouth; /ʌ/ is central and a little higher, with the jaw only moderately open and the tongue relaxed.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Half-open jaw, a short vowel, then /k/. Not 'knack'.
quests.explanation: Opening wider would turn it into 'knack', so stop at half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ has the jaw half open and the tongue mid-front; /æ/ needs the jaw dropped clearly lower, tongue low and forward, mouth wide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The l is silent. In RP the vowel is long and open.
quests.explanation: A silent l, and 'palm' and 'half' follow suit.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɑː/ is back, open and long with unrounded lips; /æ/ is front and shorter, with the tongue pushed forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent r. Oval lips, held vowel.
quests.explanation: 'Hoarse' sounds exactly the same in RP, so the spelling never helps.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔː/ is longer, higher and more strongly rounded; /ɒ/ is short, more open and only lightly rounded.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and central. Not rounded like 'put'.
quests.explanation: The u here follows 'cut', not 'put', so keep the lips unrounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Most u words take /ʌ/ (cut, bus), but a small closed set takes /ʊ/ (put, full, push). Spelling cannot decide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Before a voiced /d/ both vowels lengthen, so don't rely on length. Listen for the tension.
quests.explanation: Before a voiced consonant the short vowel lengthens too, so quality is the cue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling is mixed: ee and ea usually spell /iː/, i and y spell /ɪ/ in most words, with exceptions such as 'machine'.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A long central vowel before a dark /l/. Lips neutral.
quests.explanation: The dark /l/ makes the end heavy, but the vowel stays steady and central.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both duration and height separate the pair: lengthen and slightly raise the tongue for /ɜː/, clip and open for /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short, jaw nearly closed. A bigger gap would make 'left'.
quests.explanation: 'Left' would need a wider jaw, so keep the mouth nearly closed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Duration is similar, so rely on openness: a small mouth gap for /ɪ/, a slightly larger one for /e/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ui spelling again. Push forward and hold.
quests.explanation: Ui spells this vowel in 'fruit', 'juice' and 'suit'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: After /sw/ the a is short and rounded, like in 'want'.
quests.explanation: After w the a often signals the short rounded vowel, not the long open one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Hold /ɑː/ longer with the jaw widest; /ɒ/ is clipped with the lips slightly forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: In RP, the a before nt is long and open.
quests.explanation: A BATH word in RP. Other accents use the wide front vowel, which is not this course's target.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Drop the jaw and pull the tongue back for /ɑː/, as a doctor would ask. For /æ/ the tongue stays forward and the mouth stretches sideways.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short and relaxed despite the oo. It rhymes with 'could'.
quests.explanation: Oo before d is short in 'wood' and 'hood' but long in 'food' and 'mood'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The er spelling. Long central vowel, lips neutral.
quests.explanation: Er before a consonant usually spells this vowel in stressed syllables.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɜː/ is long, tense and central with neutral lips; /ʌ/ is short, lower and more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ough looks scary, but the vowel is the same as in 'tough'. Neutral lips.
quests.explanation: Ough alone cannot tell you the vowel: 'rough' has /ʌ/, 'cough' has /ɒ/, and 'though' has a diphthong.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Round the lips a little and drop the jaw for /ɒ/. Keep them flat and relaxed for /ʌ/, with the tongue further forward.
